title: Cost Model API v1 — Performance Budget Worksheet (latency, caching, cardinality)
content:
Owner: Thomas Baird (Perf/Cardinality)
Last review: 2026-02-18
Audience: Platform (Cost Model service), Console backend, Optimize backend, Telemetry/Analytics, SRE

Purpose
- Define the performance budget for Cost Model API v1 so Console (hot-path dashboards) and Optimize (what-if projections) have predictable latency and bounded responses.
- Translate “don’t explode cardinality” into concrete request bounds + caching rules + query patterns.
- Establish default timeouts and fallback behavior expectations for callers.

Scope (v1 endpoints)
- /v1/cost:estimate (single request estimate; used in request traces + inline views)
- /v1/cost:breakdown (aggregated breakdown for a time window; used for dashboard tables)
- /v1/cost:what_if (scenario projection; used by Optimize)

Non-goals
- This is not the billing system of record.
- This does not define pricing; only compute budgets and bounds.


A) Latency + availability targets (service-level)

Assumptions
- Cost Model API is called by internal services (Console, Optimize). Some calls are on a user-facing path.
- We must tolerate telemetry lag. When inputs are missing/stale, return partial results with explicit status flags (see “Degraded modes”).

Targets by endpoint (prod, steady state)

| Endpoint | Typical caller | Expected QPS (steady) | p50 target | p95 target | Hard timeout (server) | Caller timeout recommendation |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| estimate | Console trace drilldown, debugging tools | 150–400 | 25 ms | 80 ms | 200 ms | 250 ms |
| breakdown | Console dashboards | 30–80 | 120 ms | 450 ms | 1200 ms | 1500 ms |
| what_if | Optimize | 5–25 | 300 ms | 1200 ms | 2500 ms | 3000 ms |

Notes
- estimate must be “fast and boring”: memory-local computation + cached model/runtime parameters; no large fan-out.
- breakdown is allowed to hit pre-aggregated telemetry tables (or cached aggregates), but must have bounded result cardinality.
- what_if is explicitly slower; it may run multiple candidate computations but must still be bounded.

Availability / error budget (draft)
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for estimate + breakdown (internal).
- what_if: 99.5% monthly acceptable due to non-hot-path nature.


B) Compute budget + caching strategy

Key principle
- All endpoints must have a “cacheable core” keyed by stable inputs. Anything high-cardinality must be caller-provided or pre-aggregated upstream.

Caches in play
1) Model Catalog + runtime metadata cache (L1 in-process)
- Contents: model_id -> (arch, param_count_bucket, context_len, quant_profile_id defaults, kernel_path_id mapping), hardware_sku -> $/sec, throughput baselines
- TTL: 15 minutes
- Warmup: on deploy + periodic refresh
- Expected hit rate: > 99% after warm

2) Telemetry aggregate cache (L2 shared, e.g., redis/memcache) — for breakdown
- Key: (org_id, project_id?, env, model_id, route_id?, region, time_bucket, schema_version, group_by_set)
- TTL: 2–5 minutes for “today” buckets; 30–60 minutes for historical buckets
- Eviction: LRU; cap by per-tenant quota (to avoid a single org dominating)

3) What-if memoization (L1 + optional L2)
- Key: (org_id, base_workload_summary_hash, scenario_hash, schema_version)
- TTL: 10 minutes
- Guardrail: only memoize if the scenario passes “cheap to reuse” predicate (scenario is common and response size is small)

Cacheability rules (caller-visible)
- estimate responses include cache_status: HIT/MISS (internal header), and “inputs_resolved_at” timestamp.
- breakdown responses include “computed_from”: [cache, preagg_table, raw_rollup] and a “time_range_truncated” boolean.
- what_if responses include “confidence” and “assumption_profile_id” (not a cache signal, but used to interpret results).

Recommended caller behavior
- Console: for dashboards, prefer breakdown requests with (a) coarse time_bucket (>= 5m) and (b) small group_by sets.
- Optimize: batch what_if calls by workload_summary and dedupe scenarios client-side.


C) Cardinality constraints (hard bounds)

Why this exists
- We saw early prototypes produce “group_by everything” breakdowns that explode in both runtime and response size (and create unbounded cache keys).

Hard request bounds (enforced server-side)
- Max time range per request:
  - breakdown: 31 days (hard), 7 days recommended for interactive
  - estimate: single request only (no ranges)
  - what_if: max 24 hours of workload summary input (summarized, not raw)
- Max group_by dimensions per breakdown request: 3
- Max distinct groups returned: 200 (top-K + “other” bucket required)
- Max models per request: 10
- Max routes per request: 50 (but only if route_id is NOT in group_by)
- Max regions per request: 10
- Max quant_profile_ids per request: 5
- Max response size (serialized): 512 KB (reject or truncate with explicit “truncated” flag)

Allowed group_by dimensions (v1)
- org_id (implicit; never group_by)
- project_id (optional; not recommended unless customer is small)
- env (prod/staging)
- model_id
- route_id
- region
- deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
- quant_profile_id
- cache_status_bucket (HIT/MISS/PARTIAL; only if derived from rollups)

Explicitly disallowed as group_by (v1)
- request_id, user_id, api_key_id, prompt_hash, tool_name, function_name
- any free-form tag keys (e.g., “metadata.*”)
Reason: unbounded, high-entropy.

Top-K semantics
- When group cardinality > 200:
  - Return top 199 by total_cost, plus one “other” bucket.
  - Provide dropped_group_count.
  - Provide ordering metric (total_cost) and stable tie-breaking (lexicographic) for determinism.


D) Budget by computation stage (internal breakdown)

For estimate endpoint (target p95 <= 80 ms)
- Request validation + auth/tenancy: 5–10 ms
- Resolve model + hardware + pricing primitives (cached): 5–15 ms
- Compute prefill/decode token accounting + kv cache attribution: 10–25 ms
- Overhead allocation (simple rule): 5–15 ms
- Serialization: 2–8 ms

For breakdown endpoint (target p95 <= 450 ms)
- Auth + bounds validation: 10–20 ms
- Aggregate fetch (pre-aggregated telemetry): 60–250 ms
- Post-processing (top-K, other bucket, normalization): 30–120 ms
- Optional joins (model metadata for display names): 5–30 ms

For what_if endpoint (target p95 <= 1200 ms)
- Validate scenario + guardrails: 10–40 ms
- Workload summary normalization: 20–80 ms
- Scenario compute (batching/caching/quant deltas): 150–900 ms
- Confidence + assumption stamping: 10–60 ms


E) Degraded modes + fallback behavior

Degraded modes we expect
1) Telemetry lag / missing bucket
- behavior: return partial with status=PARTIAL_INPUTS and missing_ranges list (bounded to 20 entries)
- do NOT block waiting for telemetry catch-up

2) Cache backend unhealthy
- estimate: continue (L1 only); never depend on L2
- breakdown: fall back to direct pre-agg query path; tighten bounds (max groups 100) and set status=DEGRADED_CACHE
- what_if: continue; skip L2 memoization; tighten scenario max_candidates

3) Downstream model catalog slowdown
- behavior: use stale cache up to 60 minutes; stamp “metadata_stale=true”

Caller fallback expectations (important for Console)
- Console must have a feature-flagged fallback to existing (legacy) cost breakdown for 30 days post-launch.
- If Cost Model API p95 > 800 ms for breakdown over 10 min window, Console should reduce refresh frequency + use cached UI data.


F) Request shaping guidance (to prevent expensive patterns)

Console dashboard recommended query patterns
- Time bucket: 5m for last 24h; 1h for 7d; 1d for 31d
- group_by: model_id + route_id (avoid adding region unless the user explicitly filters)
- Always pass filters when available (model_id, route_id, region) rather than using group_by to discover everything.

Optimize what_if recommended patterns
- Provide workload summary, not raw request samples.
- Cap scenario count per request to 5.
- Prefer one scenario per call if you need low latency; batch scenarios if you accept p95 ~1.2s.


G) Open questions / decisions needed (as of 2026-02-18)
1) Do we need a separate “async breakdown job” endpoint for heavy dashboard loads?
- Proposed: not for v1; revisit if breakdown QPS > 150 sustained.

2) Should route_id be allowed in group_by by default?
- Console wants it; perf risk if customers have high route cardinality.
- Proposal: allow route_id group_by only when time_range <= 7d OR time_bucket >= 1h.

3) Response truncation semantics
- Decision needed: reject vs truncate.
- Proposal: truncate with “other” bucket, plus explicit flags. Reject only if response would exceed 2 MB.


H) Action items (next 2–3 weeks)
- [Ethan Park] Confirm endpoint timeouts + default server limits in cost-model service config. (ENG-4821)
- [Thomas Baird] Add request bounds + top-K enforcement to breakdown endpoint; include deterministic ordering tests. (ENG-4822)
- [Logan Wright] Ensure pre-aggregated telemetry tables support required group_by sets with bounded scan. (ENG-4823)
- [Chloe Martin] Update Console integration to use recommended time buckets + filters; avoid “group_by region” by default. (ENG-4825)
- [Rafael Mendes] Draft SLO + alert thresholds aligned with p95 targets and degraded-mode behavior. (ENG-4827)

Appendix: Quick checklist for PR reviews
- Does the change add a new group_by dimension? If yes, is it bounded and documented?
- Does the change increase response size risk? If yes, confirm truncation behavior + tests.
- Does the change add new cache keys? If yes, confirm key includes schema_version and has bounded cardinality.
- Does the change affect p95? If yes, include benchmark results (staging load test or microbench).
